ratings_why.fun: Reading the shop as a menu of texts makes every Recruit Phase a fresh puzzle and the board keeps changing, but two layers of text per card slow the glance.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: no tribe today treats the shop itself as the resource, wearing a unit's text without buying it and leaving a 1-gold Stock in its slot, so the folklore swap is the mechanic.

verdict_why: The core reads well and fits the fantasy; Pip Unlike, Coat-Peg Steward and Tam Twice need their rules pinned down so a player can read them.

points.text: Pip Unlike swaps four things at once (sides, diagonals, rows, Start/End of Turn), so a player can't predict what a worn text does at a glance. Keep only left and right swapping; that is the mirror-backwards joke and it reads instantly.

Coat-Peg Steward 'also wears its guise': it's unclear whether each fallen Changeling's guise stacks on the Steward or replaces the last one. Say which, for example 'adds its guise; these stack this fight'.
Tam Twice wearing a Changeling you own: does it copy that Changeling's own text only, or its guise too? Say so on the card or in the Guise rules.
Inside-Out Tod must re-wear on every sale, which can strip a guise you wanted. 'May wear it' keeps the choice readable and the inside-out coat joke intact.

The woodland fantasy lands in what the cards do: the Stock left in the shop, Penny making the enemy lose its own text, Grandfer stacking old faces. Lean on a guise badge in the UI so the second text is one tap away.

standouts.why: The Stock is the folklore made into a shop rule: you take the original, a log is left behind for 1 gold, and you can see the swap was 'fair'.
Penny Second is the turned-away duchess as a Start of Combat effect: your Changeling becomes the enemy and the enemy loses its own text. Clear and memorable.
Wicker Moll turns every Stock into a working copy; one line of text makes a whole build and reads at a glance.

weakest.why: Pip Unlike's four-way mirror is the hardest card in the tribe to read and its effect depends on which text it wears.
Cradle Foundling is just Guise on a body; fine as the seed but has nothing of its own to remember.
Grandfer Acorn can hold four layers of text, the most a player must read on one card.

flags.note: Four simultaneous swaps on worn text; hard to predict what the guise does.
Whether gathered guises stack or replace is not stated.
Wearing an owned Changeling: copies its guise or not?
1-gold Stocks carrying up to Tier 5 text with +3/+3 can fill a board cheaply.
Wiping up to four enemy texts can feel bad to the opponent; worth the owner's eye, not a lock.
Golden Lady with Grandfer and Glamour-Weaver gives a very high roll; bounded by once-a-turn limits.
